title: Select ints with composed IntPredicates

blocks.text: `IntPredicate` is `boolean test(int)`: the primitive form of `Predicate<Integer>`, with no boxing, and the type `IntStream.filter` takes. It composes with `and()`, `or()` and `negate()`, but has no static `not()` or `isEqual()`.

items: `between(int lo, int hi)` returns an `IntPredicate` for `lo <= n <= hi`.
`outside(int lo, int hi)` returns its opposite (`negate()` gives it directly).
`select(int from, int to, IntPredicate keep)` returns the values `from, from + 1, …, to` that pass `keep`.

blocks.text: Mind the bounds, and a range written backwards: `between(5, 1)` holds no number at all, so `outside(5, 1)` holds every number. The tests keep `to` below `Integer.MAX_VALUE` and every range small.

cases.says: select keeps, in order, the values of the range that pass the predicate.
between includes both of its bounds.
outside is true exactly where between is false, bounds included.
A range whose start is past its end holds no values.
between(5, 1) is not the same as between(1, 5): with lo above hi it holds no number, and outside holds all.

concepts: IntPredicate tests an int with no boxing and composes with and, or and negate.
